Looking at these decks and questions, this whole thing feels like a behavioral experiment on venture evaluation and startup decision-making.

What it looks like they're testing:

Capital Allocation Under Uncertainty: How people divide a limited pool of capital (100 units) across different tech verticals (robotics, AI security, document automation, infrastructure) when balancing potential upside against execution risk.

Traction vs. Hype: Seeing whether investors/analysts actually care more about real production ARR and granted patents (like Axonmesh) versus hype-heavy, early-stage ideas that only have waitlists or provisional patents (like Servora or Pulsegrid).

Attention to Detail: The fact-check multiple-choice questions right before the allocation prompt are almost certainly "attention checks" to make sure you're actually reading the fine print in the slides rather than just guessing.

Basically, it's measuring how structured, risk-averse, or hype-driven your investment logic is when presented with standardized startup pitches
